QUESTION:
Which other drugs interact with Lisinopril?

RESPONSE:
Lisinopril, an ACE inhibitor, has several notable drug interactions. It can increase the serum potassium levels, so concurrent use with potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g., spironolactone), or potassium-containing salt substitutes can increase the risk of hyperkalemia. Lisinopril may also interact with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), which can reduce its antihypertensive effectiveness and may increase the risk of renal impairment. Additionally, combining lisinopril with other antihypertensive agents can enhance blood pressure lowering effects, requiring dose adjustments. Lithium toxicity risk is increased when used concomitantly with lisinopril. Diuretics such as hydrochlorothiazide are commonly combined with lisinopril to improve efficacy and reduce hypokalemia risk, but careful monitoring is warranted. Always evaluate for potential drug interactions before initiating lisinopril.
